Candidate node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question's scope. That limits its answer without establishing that those applications are substantively disqualified. Candidate node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa answers only substantive qualification; its true result cannot establish actual procedural relief.

The explicit commencement date supports the date threshold, but the source does not specify a universal assessment-event or implementation-date test. Candidate node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e particularly needs clarification of the relationship between assessment and proposed implementation.

The publication date is absent, so the introductory immediate-effect wording cannot independently be reconciled with the specified Effective Date. The explicit implementation provision supports using 28 November 2025 without inventing another commencement date.

The relevant FAQs and any SFC clarification of transition treatment are missing for resolving actual procedural availability. The supplied dependency IDs have null source hashes and no identifying descriptions; neither can safely be matched to a particular missing authority. Applicable home-jurisdiction requirements would also be needed to determine home compliance in a concrete case.

These checks concern the two supplied claims only. Preservation of scope or commencement does not validate the entire relief formula. No separate home-supervision condition is expressly imposed by item (ii), and failure of its relief conditions does not independently establish an approval obligation.
